'''The Deployment Checklist''' lists every step required to deploy a new service
with docker compose. Do NOT skip any of them.

== Step 1 - verify the mount map ==

Before writing any files, verify the container's volume mounts:

<pre>
docker inspect omni-stack-omniagent-1 --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} -&gt; {{.Destination}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
</pre>

This tells you where your files will actually land. The critical point is that
the filesystem tool writes to the container path, while the compose tool validates
the host path; see [[Container Mount Map]] for the full table.

== Step 2 - check port availability ==

Do NOT use an in-container fetch to probe a host port: that only sees this
container's network namespace, and a container on the host can occupy the port
while staying invisible. Do use the compose tool to list the target project, and
check whether another compose project already owns the port.

== Step 3 - write files to paths reachable by compose ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Container path (filesystem tool) !! Host path (compose tool) !! Accessible to compose?
|-
| <code>/opt/workspace/...</code> || <code>/opt/workspace/...</code> || yes
|-
| <code>/opt/omni/...</code> || <code>/opt/workspace/omni-root/...</code> || yes, via the translated host path
|-
| <code>/app/...</code> || <code>/opt/workspace/omniagent/...</code> || yes
|}

{{OmniFact
|what=compose deployment checklist
|where=any new stack service
|status=standing rules
|source=Projects/Omniagent/Deployment-Checklist.md
}}

== Step 4 - create the compose file ==

The compose file must use a valid image (pulled from a registry or built from a
Dockerfile), map the container port to the target host port, and mount volumes
correctly with absolute or verified relative paths.

== Step 5 - deploy ==

Writing the compose file does NOT deploy it. Always call the compose tool with
<code>command="up"</code> and detached arguments:

<pre>
docker_compose(project_dir="&lt;host-abs-path&gt;", command="up", args="-d")
</pre>

The project directory is the HOST path where the compose file resides. The
service argument is only needed for <code>exec</code>, <code>stop</code> and
<code>restart</code>, not for <code>up</code> or <code>down</code>.

== Step 6 - verify ==

Check that the service is running with <code>command="ps"</code>, then verify it
responds - for example an HTTP header request from inside the composed
container. A successful <code>up -d</code> can still hide a failed port binding,
so always verify with both the process list and a health check.

== Anti-patterns ==

* '''Scope creep during deployment''': do not upgrade infrastructure while
  deploying; that is a separate task.
* '''Not verifying after compose''': the port binding can fail silently.
* '''Writing the compose file without deploying''': the file is inert until
  <code>up</code> runs.
* '''Probing a host port from inside the container''': the network namespace
  hides other projects.
* '''Calling the compose tool by the wrong name''': the registered bare name is
  <code>compose</code> is NOT valid; use the registered tool name.
